ImageDescription.value: This figure depicts the tracks of representative radial null geodesics in the Born coordinate chart for Minkowski spacetime, in which the world lines (nongeodesic timelike curves) of Langevin observers appear as vertical lines. Langevin observers rotate with angular velocity ω about the axis of symmetry r = 0. In an ordinary cylindrical chart, these appear as helices. The figure shows that, as depicted in the Born chart, Langevin observers see a central observer "displaced from his true position" because they must look ahead to compensate for their motion (the green outbound radial null geodesic). Whereas a stationary observer at the center r = 0 has to look behind to see the ring riding Langevin observer (the red inbound radial null geodesic).

Categories.value: Special relativity|Geodesic (mathematics)|Rotation|Self-published work|Valid SVG created with Gnuplot:Diagrams|16-fold rotational symmetry

ImageDescription.value: Null geodesics depicted in the Born chart between ring riding Langenvin observers. Null geodesics propagating with the rotation are bent inward (green curve), null geodesics propagating against the rotation are bent outward (red curve). Null geodesics between opposite Langevin observers (L<sub>1</sub> and L<sub>3</sub>) bend symmetrically around the center of rotation.
